evidence.note: Token endpoint uses plaintext HTTP, which is unsafe.
Userinfo path is not under the tenant path used by the other endpoints.
Issuer matches the configured value, so this is not an issuer mismatch.

output.fix: Fix the discovery document at the source so that every endpoint, token_endpoint included, is an https URL on the same tenant-scoped authority as the issuer. Check that the userinfo_endpoint belongs to this tenant. Remove 'plain' from code_challenge_methods_supported and have clients use S256 only. Then reload the document. AADSTS50049 means Entra doesn't recognise the instance or authority. Confirm that the host is a real Entra authority (login.microsoftonline.com) or a registered custom domain, and that the tenant ID in the path is valid. Don't relax the https requirement or the issuer check to get around the error.

alternatives.why_not: The issuer in the document equals the configured issuer.
The error is raised while loading the discovery document, before any client configuration is evaluated.

questions: Is login.example.com a registered custom domain or authority for this Entra tenant, or is it a proxy or mock?
Was the document fetched directly from the authority's /.well-known/openid-configuration, or has it been rewritten by an intermediary?
